name: TX-36
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans 12 points Republican, a strong structural advantage for the GOP
Babin has raised about $1.0M with $909K on hand; Hart has raised nothing
Incumbent was renominated without difficulty; no polls or expert ratings flag any competition
Prediction markets price Republican win odds near 93%
model.rationale: A twelve-point Republican lean, Babin's incumbency, and a roughly million-dollar cash edge against a challenger who has raised no money all point to an easy Republican hold. With no polls or ratings suggesting the race is contested, the main uncertainty is simply how large the margin gets.
model.watch: Any late Democratic fundraising, outside spending, or a poll showing a single-digit race would be the first sign this is becoming competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 36th District, anchored in the East Texas pineywoods, leans about twelve points Republican at the presidential level, and Brian Babin has held the seat since 2017. He enters the general election renominated without difficulty, with roughly one million dollars raised and more than 900,000 dollars on hand. Democrat Rhonda Hart has reported no fundraising and no cash on hand, leaving her without the resources typically needed to contest a district this red.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets put Republican chances at about ninety-three percent. The combination of a strong partisan lean, an established incumbent, and a completely unfunded challenger points to a comfortable Republican hold. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of independent polling, which keeps the margin estimate broader than in well-surveyed districts.
